concept.name: Ultima
concept.definition: Ultima is a third-order sensitivity of an option's value: the rate of change of volga (vomma) with respect to volatility, i.e., the third derivative of value with respect to volatility alone. It measures the convexity of vega convexity — how volga exposure itself shifts as implied volatility changes.
concept.intuition: Ultima is the volatility analogue of speed: it tells deep volatility books how their volga will mutate if volatility itself keeps rising or collapsing.
concept.mechanics: Ultima = d(volga)/d(sigma) = d3V/d(sigma)3. It matters only for portfolios with large volga exposure — typically books concentrated in OTM wings — where second-order estimates of vega change themselves become unreliable across large volatility moves.
concept.failure_modes: Ultima sits at the edge of practical risk measurement: third-order-in-volatility terms are swamped by smile, skew dynamics, and quote discreteness, so computed ultima is a model artifact as much as a risk number.
concept.misconceptions: Ultima is not a measure of tail event probability — it is a smooth-model derivative that says nothing directly about crash risk, only about how wing-book sensitivities bend with volatility.
concept.example: A wing-heavy book whose volga rises as volatility rises has negative or positive ultima depending on the smile region; risk managers use it only to bound how wrong their volga estimate could be after a 10-point vol shock.
